title: The Women's T20 World Cup Starts Tomorrow. India's First Match Is Against Pakistan.
excerpt: Harmanpreet Kaur leads a squad with seven World Cup veterans and three debutants across six venues in England. Here is everything NRIs need to know.
body:
The ICC Women's T20 World Cup begins on Thursday, June 12 in England. Twelve teams, six venues, twenty-four days. India, drawn in Group A alongside Australia, South Africa, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and the Netherlands, will open their campaign against Pakistan at Edgbaston in Birmingham on Sunday, June 14.

It is a fixture that needs no introduction. The rivalry between the two women's teams has intensified over the past three years, and a World Cup stage in England — where the South Asian diaspora will flood the stands — makes it one of the most anticipated group-stage matches of the tournament.

## India's Squad

Harmanpreet Kaur captains the side for what could be her final World Cup. At 37, the right-hander has played more Women's T20 World Cups than any other Indian cricketer, and a strong performance in England would cement her legacy as the most decorated captain in Indian women's cricket history.

The full squad: Harmanpreet Kaur (c), Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Jemimah Rodrigues, Bharti Fulmali, Deepti Sharma, Richa Ghosh, Shree Charani, Yastika Bhatia, Nandani Sharma, Arundhati Reddy, Renuka Singh, Kranti Gaud, Shreyanka Patil, and Radha Yadav.

Smriti Mandhana, who enters the tournament as the ICC's top-ranked T20I batter, is India's most reliable run-scorer. Shafali Verma provides the explosive start at the top, while Jemimah Rodrigues anchors the middle order. Richa Ghosh, one of the cleanest hitters in women's cricket, adds finishing firepower.

The bowling attack is built around Renuka Singh's pace and Deepti Sharma's off-spin. Shreyanka Patil adds left-arm spin variety, and Radha Yadav provides the slow left-arm option that has been a staple of India's T20 bowling for half a decade.

## The Group of Death

Group A is stacked. Australia, the most successful team in Women's T20 World Cup history, are led by Sophie Molineux after Alyssa Healy's retirement. South Africa, semi-finalists in the 2023 edition, bring Laura Wolvaardt's consistent batting and Shabnim Ismail's pace. Bangladesh, fresh from their qualifier campaign, have improved dramatically under Nigar Sultana's captaincy.

Even the Netherlands, appearing in their second World Cup, have capable players in Babette de Leede and Phebe Molkenboer.

India's schedule in the group stage:

- **June 14**: India vs Pakistan — Edgbaston, Birmingham (2:30 PM BST)
- **June 17**: India vs Netherlands — Headingley, Leeds (2:30 PM BST)
- **June 21**: India vs South Africa — Old Trafford, Manchester (2:30 PM BST)
- **June 25**: India vs Bangladesh — Old Trafford, Manchester (2:30 PM BST)

The top four teams from each group advance to the Super Eight stage, which begins on June 27.

## What the Diaspora Should Know

For NRIs in the United Kingdom, this is the most accessible women's cricket tournament in years. All matches are played at established Test venues — Edgbaston, Headingley, Old Trafford, the Rose Bowl, Lord's, and the County Ground in Bristol. Tickets are priced between £10 and £30 for group-stage matches, a fraction of what men's international cricket in England typically costs.

The India-Pakistan match at Edgbaston on June 14 has already sold out. Secondary market prices are running at three to four times face value. The city of Birmingham, home to one of the largest South Asian communities in the UK, is expecting one of the most charged atmospheres of the tournament.

For those watching from North America, all matches will be streamed on Willow TV and available via the cricket streaming package. Start times for India's group matches fall between 9:30 AM and 10:30 AM Eastern, making them accessible for early-morning viewing on the East Coast and convenient breakfast television on the West Coast.

## India's World Cup Record

India have reached the semi-finals of the Women's T20 World Cup four times and the final once — in 2020, when they lost to Australia at the MCG. The team has never won the tournament. With the women's game now part of the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics qualification pathway, this World Cup carries weight beyond the trophy itself.

Harmanpreet's team enters as the third-ranked T20I side in the world, behind Australia and England. Their recent form has been strong — a series win in South Africa and a dominant performance in the Asia Cup — but converting group-stage promise into knockout-stage wins has been the persistent challenge.

## Key Players to Watch

**Smriti Mandhana** is the tournament's most complete batter. Her ability to play pace and spin with equal fluency makes her dangerous on English pitches where the ball moves. She averages over 30 in T20Is and has seven half-centuries in World Cups.

**Deepti Sharma** does the dual job. She bowls her quota of restriction in the powerplay and middle overs, and bats at number six or seven with the composure of someone higher up the order. Her match awareness is India's hidden strength.

**Renuka Singh** swings the new ball both ways. In English conditions, where cloud cover and green pitches can assist seam bowling, she could be India's most potent weapon in the powerplay.

The tournament opener between hosts England and Sri Lanka takes place at Edgbaston on Thursday, June 12 at 6:30 PM BST. India's wait begins two days later, under the same floodlights, against the same fierce opponent.
